query: Microsoft capital expenditure data center AI spending latest quarter
normalized: ai capital center data expenditure microsoft quarter spending

output.content:
Microsoft’s latest reported quarter is **FY2026 Q4, ended June 30, 2026**. [[1]]

- **Capital expenditures were $41.0 billion** in the quarter, including the impact of higher component pricing. [[2]]
- About **two-thirds of capex—approximately $27.3 billion—went to short-lived assets**, primarily CPUs and GPUs; management said this reflected customer demand for both AI and non-AI infrastructure. [[2]]
- The remaining roughly **$13.7 billion** was directed to long-lived assets, while **finance leases totaled $5.6 billion**, primarily for large data-center sites. [[2]]
- **Cash paid for property, plant and equipment was $35.8 billion**, and free cash flow was **$19.6 billion**, with elevated capex cited as the reason for the lower conversion. [[2]]
- For the following quarter, Microsoft guided to **more than $50 billion of capex**, inclusive of the effect of a lease reclassification tied to changes in data-center asset useful lives. [[2]]
- Management said its **calendar-2026 capex expectation is approximately $175 billion** after the expected migration of some future data-center leases from finance to operating leases; the underlying investment outlook was otherwise unchanged. [[2]]
- The spending supports a cloud-and-AI business that reached **$59.3 billion of Microsoft Cloud revenue in the quarter, up 27% year over year**, while Azure exceeded **$100 billion of annual revenue** in FY2026. [[1]] [[2]]
